newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom dominates resilient German share market.
newsitem.headline: Telekom dominates resilient German share market.

text.p: German shares got the week off to a surprisingly steady start on Monday, shrugging off further declines in the dollar in early trade as selected blue chip stocks led by Deutsche Telekom AG posted firm gains.
The DAX index opened 13.13 points, or 0.4 percent lower, at 3,549.28 points, but the decline merely reflected a late fall in IBIS electronic dealings in after-bourse hours on Friday.
The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day electronic trade in the 30 blue-chip DAX shares, was up around 0.4 percent.
Deutsche Telekom, benefitting from interest ahead of its annual news conference on Tuesday and other factors, extended gains set Friday to set a new all-time high of 41.95 marks in early trade.
The shares, leading turnover volumes, were up 4.4 percent at 41.70 marks at 0842 GMT.
Some dealers were sceptical whether the broad market could remain resilient through the day. At 1.6841 marks, the dollar was notably feeble, but viewed as still in an acceptable range.
"With such a limited focus, it's hard to be confident. I could see the dollar impact gaining a bit more force as the day goes on," said one.
Telekom's surge was partly because it is approaching a six-month deadline on May 19, after which its shares can be sold without incurring tax, dealers noted.
A report in Der Spiegel magazine that the company was moving into commercial television in a bid to turn to profit on its cable business was also well received.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG also continued its recent advance after announcing its first ever first quarter profit last week. It shares were up 10 pfennigs at 28.20 marks.
